type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Craft
description: Adilabad Dokra is a traditional tribal metal craft from Telangana made using the ancient lost-wax (cire perdue) casting technique. Artisans from the Woj community create brass objects such as idols of local deities, animals, jewelry, bells, lamps, and decorative items. Each piece is unique, as replicas are nearly impossible. The craft has historical roots dating back thousands of years, with evidence linked to tribal traditions and ancient practices like those seen in Mohenjo-daro. It is labor-intensive, follows traditional designs with some modern adaptations, and is widely valued in domestic and international markets.

type of product: Non Food Products Extraction / Agate
description: Agates of Cambay are semi-precious stones made of silica and classified under quartz and chalcedony. They are formed in volcanic rock cavities and found in various colors, patterns, and forms such as banded, moss, and geode agates. These stones are used for jewelry, ornaments, and decoration. They are durable (Mohs hardness ~7) and widely available. Agates are also associated with emotional, physical, and metaphysical uses such as stress relief, protection, and confidence building, though these are belief-based. Variants like black agate, banded agate, and moss agate have specific characteristics and uses.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Carpet
description: Agra Durrie is a traditional flat-woven carpet from Agra made using cotton and other fibers. The craft has historical roots linked to ancient and Mughal periods. Production involves a structured supply chain including traders, master weavers, and workers. Master weavers produce carpets using family or hired labor, while workers contribute skilled labor without capital investment. These durable carpets are used in households and are known for their practical designs and traditional weaving techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Stone carving product
description: Allagadda Stone Carving is a traditional craft from Andhra Pradesh where artisans carve sandstone and black stone into idols and sculptures based on ancient Shilpa Sastra principles in Vijayanagara style. The stones are locally sourced, semi-hard, durable, and heat-resistant, allowing detailed and large-scale carvings. Artisans use traditional tools like chisels, hammers, and polishing materials, and typically work on a single piece at a time. The craft is highly skilled, passed through generations, and recognized for its precision, religious significance, and demand in domestic and international markets.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Coir yarn
description: Alleppey Coir is a traditional industry in Kerala that produces coir products from coconut fiber, including mats, ropes, and carpets. Initially developed by European enterprises, it later became decentralized after independence into thousands of small-scale units. Artisans spin, dye, and weave coir using traditional methods in household and cottage industries. The sector includes exporters, cooperatives, and workers, supported by the Coir Board for standardization, quality control, and welfare. The products are durable and widely exported.

type of product: Non Food Products Leather and leather based products / Puppet
description: Andhra Pradesh Leather Puppetry, known as Tholu Bommalata, is an ancient performing art dating back to at least the 3rd century BCE. It uses intricately designed leather puppets to depict stories from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata. The craft is practiced in regions like Nimmalakunta and Narsaraopet. Artisans have adapted by creating decorative items such as lampshades, wall hangings, and partitions while preserving traditional techniques like detailed punching work. The craft remains a hereditary art form passed through generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Applique (Khatwa) Work of Bihar is a traditional fabric craft practiced mainly by women in Sitamarhi and Madhubani. It involves stitching pieces of cloth onto a base fabric to create decorative and narrative designs. Originally used for functional stitching of layered cloth, it evolved into an artistic expression depicting mythology, nature, and contemporary life. Products include wall hangings, cushion covers, garments, and decorative textiles. The craft reflects cultural themes influenced by local life, media, and personal experiences.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk
description: Arani Silk is a traditional silk weaving craft from Tamil Nadu known for producing high-quality sarees using mulberry silk and zari. The craft has historical references in colonial records and involves multiple processes such as dyeing, warping, sizing, and weaving. Production includes preparing warp and weft, dyeing with color-fixing techniques, and weaving on looms to produce sarees of various lengths. Unique features include detailed pallu designs and the use of local water that enhances fabric shine. The craft is labor-intensive and traditionally family-based.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Metal mirror
description: Aranmula Kannadi is a unique handmade metal mirror made in Kerala using a special alloy of copper and tin. Unlike glass mirrors, it provides reflection from a polished metal surface. The craft is traditionally practiced by a limited number of artisan families and involves precise alloy composition and polishing techniques. It is known for its uniqueness and cultural significance.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Carving wood craft
description: Arumbavur Wood Carvings is a traditional craft from Tamil Nadu involving detailed carving of wood into temple cars, idols, and decorative items. The craft originated from artisans who migrated and settled in Arumbavur and follows ancient Shilpa Sastra guidelines. Various woods like mango, teak, and rosewood are used, and artisans rely on traditional tools instead of machines. The work is highly detailed, labor-intensive, and carried out in stages by multiple artisans. The craft is historically significant and passed down through generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Printed fabric
description: Bagh Prints are a traditional hand block printing craft practiced in Bagh village of Madhya Pradesh, known for their use of natural dyes and hand-carved wooden blocks. The process involves printing geometric and floral motifs on cotton and silk fabrics using vegetable-based colors, primarily red and black, followed by washing in river water to enhance color fastness.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Printing
description: Traditional hand block printing practiced in Bagru for over 300 years, represented by artisan groups engaged in continuous production and trade of printed textiles.

Product name: Balaramapuram Sarees and Fine Cotton Fabrics
type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton sarees
description: Balaramapuram sarees are fine handwoven cotton textiles from Kerala, produced using traditional pit looms with high-quality yarn. Known for their simplicity, durability, and elegant golden zari borders (kasavu), these fabrics reflect a centuries-old weaving tradition and are widely used for sarees, mundu, and veshti.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: Baluchari sarees are richly woven silk sarees from West Bengal, distinguished by intricate motifs depicting mythological scenes, historical narratives, and cultural themes on the pallu. Produced using jacquard looms, these sarees are known for their artistic storytelling and fine silk craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Silk sarees
description: Handloom silk brocades and sarees produced in Varanasi under the guidance of handloom authorities and traditional weaving practices.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Figurine
description: A traditional enamel craft of Banaras practiced for generations, supporting around 100 artisan families. Known for preserving cultural heritage, though facing challenges from rising material costs and competition from cheaper imitations.

type of product: Non Food Products / Animal-based fibres and textile
description: Banaras Hand Block Print textiles are traditional fabrics produced in Varanasi using hand-carved wooden blocks and natural or synthetic dyes. The craft is characterized by intricate floral and Mughal-inspired motifs printed on silk and other fabrics, reflecting the rich textile heritage of the region

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Door plates cutlery temple decorations
description: A traditional handcrafted metal embossing (repoussé) art of Varanasi practiced for generations by artisan communities. It involves shaping and decorating thin metal sheets using chasing and embossing techniques with detailed motifs. The process is entirely manual, using traditional tools and multiple stages including design transfer, embossing, heating, cleaning, and polishing. The craft is historically significant, linked to temple art and heritage structures, and continues as a primary livelihood for artisan families.

type of product: Non Food Products / Wooden products / Carved wood - handicraft
description: Banaras Wood Carving is a traditional handicraft of Varanasi involving the shaping and carving of wood into decorative and utilitarian items. Artisans create finely detailed designs on furniture, toys, and religious artifacts, often finished with lacquer work and vibrant colors.

type of product: Non Food Products / Others / Embroidery - handicraft
description: Banaras Zardozi is an elaborate form of hand embroidery practiced in Varanasi, using gold and silver threads along with beads and sequins on fabrics like silk and velvet. Known for its intricate patterns and royal appeal, it has historically been associated with garments for royalty and ceremonial wear

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Craft
description: Bankura Panchmura Terracotta Craft is a traditional clay art from West Bengal, especially known for the iconic Bankura horse. Crafted using locally available clay and fired in kilns, these terracotta figures are valued for their stylized forms and cultural significance in rituals and decoration.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Figurine
description: Traditional iron craft of Bastar practiced by artisans, reflecting longstanding metalworking traditions.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Carving craft
description: Traditional wood carving craft of Bastar with established methods of production and recognized uniqueness, practiced by local artisans.

Product name: Bell Metal Ware of Datia and Tikamgarh
type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Bell
description: Traditional bell metal craft using the lost-wax casting process. Artisans create mud moulds, apply wax designs, and cast metal alloys such as brass, zinc, copper, and silver. The process involves mould preparation, wax modeling, furnace heating, metal pouring, finishing, and polishing, often using recycled metal materials.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Handicraft
description: A traditional metal casting craft of West Bengal using the ancient lost-wax (cire perdue) technique. Practiced in districts like Bankura, Purulia, and Bardhaman, it involves clay core making, wax modeling, moulding, de-waxing, metal pouring, and finishing using materials like brass, clay, wax, and natural resins.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Painting
description: A traditional scroll painting art of West Bengal depicting religious and secular themes through narrative sequences. Produced mainly in districts like Paschim Medinipur, Bankura, and Birbhum, it features vertical or horizontal scrolls and single panels, often accompanied by songs. Natural dyes and handmade tools are used in its production.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk sarees
description: Traditional silk saree and joda produced under the supervision of the Directorate of Textiles and Handloom, Odisha.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk
description: Bhagalpur Silk, also known as Tussar silk, is a natural silk produced in Bihar using wild silkworm cocoons. Renowned for its texture, durability, and natural golden sheen, it is widely used for sarees, shawls, and other garments, making Bhagalpur known as the “Silk City” of India.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton carpet
description: A traditional handwoven cotton carpet originating in Bhavani, developed since the 16th century. Known for its multicolored patterns, korvai weaving technique, and use of vegetable dyes, it is produced on pit looms by skilled artisans. The craft supports thousands of workers and is widely used for household, ceremonial, and export purposes.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Craft
description: A traditional metal craft from Bidar involving casting a zinc-copper alloy, engraving designs, and inlaying silver. The metal is treated with a special soil solution to create a distinctive black surface contrasting with silver inlay, followed by polishing to achieve a lustrous finish.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Pottery
description: A traditional pottery of Jaipur made from a quartz-based ceramic body, known for its hand-painted designs, low shrinkage, and single firing process. It is durable, non-cracking, and suited to hot, dry climates, though production is labor-intensive.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Music instrument
description: A traditional string instrument originating from the 16th-century Bobbili Samasthanam, known for its distinctive construction and sound quality. It is crafted through an elaborate manual process ensuring precise thickness and structure.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: A traditional handloom textile of Odisha combining tie-dye (ikat) techniques with intricate motifs. Originating from weaving traditions dating back to ancient times and developed through Bhulia weavers, it features unique anchal designs, natural and later chemical dyes, and is produced through complex processes of tying, dyeing, and weaving.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Craft
description: A traditional brass craft from Budithi involving both casting and sheet-work techniques. The process includes ritual practices, sheet preparation, beating, casting, welding, and finishing, producing distinctive vessels known for their characteristic sound and structure.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Bells and brass craft
description: A brass and bell metal craft practiced for about 200 years in villages of Andhra Pradesh. It involves shaping and joining brass sheets, casting components, and finishing vessels like Bindelu, distinguished by unique construction and decorative rings made using specialized techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton home furnishing
description: A traditional handloom textile industry of Kannur with a history of over 400 years, producing cotton home furnishings such as bed linen, curtains, and upholstery. Known for high-quality dyeing, durable fabrics, and diverse weaving techniques, it uses processes like scouring, bleaching, dyeing, and weaving on pit looms.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Shalw
description: Chakhesang Shawls are traditional handwoven textiles of the Chakhesang Naga tribe of Nagaland, characterized by bold geometric patterns and symbolic motifs. Woven using indigenous techniques and natural fibers, these shawls represent social identity, cultural heritage, and tribal status.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Shawl
description: Traditional shawls of the Chakhesang community in Nagaland, made from cotton and natural fibers like nettle and jute. The craft involves hand spinning, natural dyeing from local plants, and intricate weaving techniques reflecting cultural heritage and distinctive motifs.

type of product: Non Food Products / Leather and leather based products / Shoe - handicraft
description: Chamba Chappal is a traditional handcrafted footwear from Himachal Pradesh made using locally sourced leather and hand stitching techniques. Known for its durability and comfort, the footwear often features simple yet elegant designs reflecting the cultural heritage of the region.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Embroidery
description: A traditional embroidered textile from Chamba, Himachal Pradesh, inspired by Pahari miniature painting and developed under royal patronage. Made on hand-spun fabric using the unique double-sided ‘dorukha’ satin stitch, it features mythological and cultural motifs with detailed craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Silk sarees
description: Traditional kosa silk textiles associated with tribal and handloom weavers, produced through generational practices, though facing challenges due to limited institutional support.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: A traditional handwoven fabric known for its sheer texture, transparency, and fine quality yarn. Distinguished by intricate handwoven butti motifs using gold, silver, or synthetic zari, it is produced on handlooms by skilled artisans and valued for its durability and elegance.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products
description: Channapatna Toys are traditional wooden toys made in Karnataka using soft ivory wood and natural dyes. Crafted using a lathe-turning technique and finished with eco-friendly lacquer, these toys are known for their vibrant colors, smooth finish, and child-safe materials.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Lacquerware toys
description: Channapatna Toys and Dolls are lacquered wooden artifacts produced in Karnataka using traditional techniques involving natural dyes and hand-turning on a lathe. These toys are distinguished by their glossy finish, bright colors, and safe, non-toxic materials.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton sarees
description: Chendamangalam Dhoties and Set Mundu are traditional handwoven cotton garments from Kerala produced using fine yarn on pit looms. Known for their simplicity, durability, and characteristic kasavu borders, these textiles are an integral part of Kerala’s cultural attire.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Painting
description: A traditional scroll painting art from Telangana dating back to at least the 17th century, influenced by Vijayanagara and South Indian styles. It depicts mythological and community narratives, produced in Cheriyal village using established artistic traditions.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Craft
description: A traditional basketry craft of Chettinad made from locally available palm leaves. Originally used in rituals, it is characterized by unique weaving styles and colors, and produced through manual techniques supporting rural women artisans.

type of product: Non Food Products Extraction / Stone
description: A historic sandstone associated with the Chunar region, used in forts, temples, and sculptures since ancient times. Linked to significant historical periods including Mauryan and Mughal eras, it continues to be used in stone carving and construction with both traditional and modern methods.

type of product: Non Food Products / Processed minerals / Pottery - handicraft
description: Chunar Glaze Pottery is a traditional ceramic craft from Uttar Pradesh characterized by its distinctive glazed surface and earthy tones. Made using locally available clay and fired in kilns, the pottery includes decorative and utilitarian items with smooth finishes and durable quality.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Grinder
description: A mechanized kitchen appliance developed in Coimbatore in 1955, evolving from traditional grinding stones. Known for its specialized stone components, skilled manufacturing, and various types such as conventional, tilting, and tabletop models, it is widely used for preparing batter and supports a large local industry.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton fabric
description: A traditional handloom craft from Dhalapathar village practiced by the Rangani community for over a century. Originally known for sarees, it evolved into door curtains (parda) from 1936, using cotton yarn, natural dyes, and intricate weaving techniques depicting cultural and temple motifs.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: A traditional cotton saree from West Bengal woven on fly shuttle pit looms using fine cotton yarn. Known for its durable texture, contrast borders, and motifs created with dobby or jacquard techniques, it features characteristic color patterns and designs.

Product name: Dharmavaram Handloom Pattu Sarees and Paavadas
type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Silk sarees
description: A traditional handloom silk textile from Andhra Pradesh with historical references to temple art. Made using pure silk and zari, it involves processes such as degumming, dyeing, twisting, and pit loom weaving, producing durable sarees known for rich colors, intricate designs, and ceremonial use.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Locks
description: A traditional handcrafted lock industry of Dindigul with over a century of history. Known for manual production, unique key codes, diverse shapes, and high durability, these locks are distinguished from machine-made alternatives and widely used for security purposes.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Stone carving product
description: Durgi Stone Carvings are traditional sculptures produced in Andhra Pradesh using locally sourced limestone. Artisans create finely detailed idols, panels, and decorative pieces, reflecting religious themes and intricate craftsmanship passed down through generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Leather and leather based products / Vegetable tanned leather
description: A traditional vegetable-tanned leather developed during the colonial period, using natural tannins such as myrobalan and avaram bark. Produced mainly in Tamil Nadu, it is known for its light beige color, durability, and distinctive fragrance, with processes involving soaking, liming, tanning, and finishing.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Toy
description: Etikoppaka Toys are handcrafted wooden toys from Andhra Pradesh made using soft wood and natural dyes. Produced using traditional lathe techniques and finished with lacquer, these eco-friendly toys are known for their smooth texture, durability, and vibrant colors.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton print
description: Farrukhabad Prints are traditional hand block printed textiles from Uttar Pradesh known for their intricate floral and geometric patterns. Printed on cotton fabrics using carved wooden blocks and natural dyes, the craft reflects a rich heritage of textile printing.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Craft
description: A traditional glassware industry centered in Firozabad, known for handcrafted bangles and diverse glass products. Production involves specialized craftsmen performing distinct processes, using materials like silica and soda ash, with techniques including mouth blowing and manual finishing passed through generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: A traditional handloom saree from Andhra Pradesh known for its unique interlocking technique joining body, border, and pallu. Made using silk or cotton with zari work, it features intricate designs, vibrant colors, and is produced through skilled manual weaving rooted in a 200-year-old tradition.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Flower
description: Pandanus odoratissimus (kewda/ketki) has been referenced in ancient Sanskrit texts and used for worship, ornamentation, and perfumery for over two millennia. Cultivated mainly in the Ganjam district of Odisha, its flowers are harvested early during the monsoon and immediately processed by hydrodistillation in local distilleries. The kewda perfume industry, established about 200 years ago, produces attar, water, and essential oil (rooh), primarily from male flowers rich in aromatic compounds. The plant also supports handicrafts from leaves and roots, has medicinal uses, and provides ecological benefits such as soil binding and coastal stabilization. Its high fragrance is influenced by the region’s sandy soil, climate, and traditional cultivation and processing methods.

type of product: Non Food Products Other vegetal-based products / Essential oil
description: Ganjam Kewda Rooh is a highly fragrant essential oil extracted from fresh kewda flowers through traditional hydro-distillation (Deg-Bhabka method). Production is concentrated in Odisha’s Ganjam district, especially during the peak season from July to September. Approximately 30–40 grams of oil are obtained from 1000 flowers, with yield varying by season, location, and flower quality. The oil’s distinctive fragrance is attributed to the region’s sandy soil, climate, and genetic characteristics of the plant. It contains multiple aromatic compounds, with quality assessed by gas chromatography, and is widely used in perfumery, flavoring, and related industries.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Craft cards
description: Mysore Ganjifa cards are traditional hand-painted playing cards with origins linked to Persian influences and Mughal patronage, later flourishing under the Mysore rulers, especially Mummadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar. Historically used in royal courts, the craft incorporates themes from mythology, epics, and court life. Cards are made from materials such as handmade paper, cloth, ivory, or palm leaf, and painted using natural dyes derived from minerals, plants, and other sources. The production involves layering, sketching, painting, embossing, and varnishing, often with intricate iconography and fine detailing. Each deck is handmade and unique, reflecting skilled craftsmanship, cultural narratives, and regional artistic traditions.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Jute wall hanging
description: Jute wall hangings have been produced for over 50 years in Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh, by artisan communities including Muslim, Scheduled Caste, and OBC groups. The craft uses natural jute yarn and traditional Banaras weaving techniques such as Naka-Jala-Taka, without Jacquard or electricity. Designs include religious figures, landscapes, animals, and modern motifs, created with 10–20 colors through manual skill. The products are eco-friendly, entirely handmade, and dyed using traditional methods. The cluster involves thousands of artisans and contributes significantly to local income, though production methods and designs remain largely traditional with limited modernization.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk fabric
description: Gopalpur Tussar Fabrics are handwoven silk textiles from Odisha made using tussar silk derived from wild silkworms. Known for their rich texture, natural sheen, and durability, these fabrics often feature traditional motifs and vibrant colors.

type of product: Non Food Products / Processed minerals
description: Gorakhpur terracotta is a traditional clay art form with origins tracing back to the Indus Valley Civilization (2600–1700 BC), where pottery, figurines, and earthenware were widely produced. Archaeological findings from sites like Mohenjodaro and Harappa highlight its historical significance, including fertility-related figurines. The craft involves shaping and firing clay to create items such as pottery, sculptures, bowls, and decorative objects, reflecting a long-standing tradition of earthen artistry in India.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk
description: Guledgudd Khana is a traditional handwoven textile from Karnataka made using a blend of silk and cotton yarns. Characterized by small checkered patterns and contrasting borders, it is commonly used for garments and reflects the region’s distinctive weaving tradition.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: Habaspuri sarees originate from the Kalahandi district of Odisha, traditionally woven by tribal and Scheduled Caste weavers. Initially produced in Habaspur village and now in surrounding areas, these sarees have a long-standing cultural significance and are used as ceremonial bridal attire. The weaving style reflects tribal traditions, featuring distinctive extra warp temple (Kumbha) motifs arranged longitudinally on borders and extra weft designs on the anchal. Fabrics are made from cotton or silk using Jalla technique on pit looms, with natural and synthetic dyes derived from local forest resources. The craft involves detailed processes such as degumming, dyeing, warping, and weaving, resulting in textiles that embody regional identity, traditional motifs, and skilled craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Jasmine flower
description: Hadagali Mallige is a jasmine variety cultivated in Karnataka for 300–400 years, with documented use since the Vijayanagara Empire. Known for its strong fragrance and mild volatile oil content, it is primarily used for decorative purposes and making garlands, especially for marriages. Its unique characteristics arise from the genetic traits of the plant and the specific geographical conditions of the Hadagali region, particularly sandy red soil and dry climate. The crop is propagated through stem cuttings, grown with locally prepared organic manure, and begins flowering after one year, with peak yield from the second year. The flower contributes significantly to the local economy, supporting thousands of workers and generating substantial annual turnover, and is mainly cultivated in and around Hoovina Hadagali in Bellary district.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Carpet
description: Handmade carpets from Bhadohi, India, produced using traditional weaving techniques with vegetal-based fibres.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cloth
description: Hmaram is a traditional handwoven cloth of the Hmar tribe in Mizoram, historically referenced in texts from the early 20th century and earlier. It is a skirt or sarong worn by women, especially during festivals and dances, and valued as a cultural garment. Traditionally made from handspun cotton dyed with natural substances like soot and plant-based dyes, it features intricate motifs such as Kawkpui zikzial and Lenbuangthuam. The cloth is woven on a loin loom using warp-faced plain weave with supplementary yarns for designs. Production involves starching yarn with rice water, natural dyeing, and skilled manual weaving. High-quality pieces require experienced weavers to produce clear and complete motifs.

type of product: Non Food Products / Vegetal-based fibres and textile
description: Idu Mishmi textiles originate from the Idu Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh and are traditionally woven for daily use and special occasions. The textiles use natural colours such as black, red, and white, with patterns inspired by nature, featuring geometric motifs like diamonds and triangles. Yarn is traditionally extracted from wild nettle plants, processed with ash and water, and dyed using plant materials. Cotton and wool are also used, often sourced through trade. Weaving is done on local looms, producing durable, moisture-absorbing fabrics. The craft involves specialized terminology and tools, and knowledge of traditional dyeing is now limited to certain regions.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: Ilkal Sarees are traditional handwoven sarees from Karnataka known for their distinctive weaving technique where the body and pallu are woven separately and joined together. Made using cotton and silk yarns, these sarees feature characteristic borders and geometric patterns reflecting regional craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Tie dye
description: Jamnagari Bandhani is an ancient tie-dye textile tradition from Gujarat, particularly Kachchh and Jamnagar, with origins possibly linked to Sindh. Historical evidence dates back to ancient India, including references in Ajanta cave paintings (6th century AD) and classical texts like Harshacharita. The technique involves resist dyeing by tying fabric to create intricate patterns, often using bright colours and dotted designs. Traditionally used for ceremonial and daily wear by various communities, the craft is known for its unique patterns created through skilled manual tying and dyeing processes.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Wool shawl
description: Kachchh shawls are traditional handwoven wool textiles from Gujarat, rooted in India’s ancient handloom heritage. They feature distinctive motifs such as Chaumukh, Dholki, and Wankia, created using extra weft techniques. Shawls, stoles, and dhabdas are produced in standard sizes with colourful borders and patterns on natural or dyed wool. Value additions include tie-dye and embroidery by artisans across villages. Production involves handloom weaving, yarn preparation, and finishing with tassels, washing, and ironing. These textiles are sold in local and international markets and reflect both cultural significance and skilled craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk
description: Kancheepuram silk sarees originate from Tamil Nadu and have historical roots dating back to the Mauryan period. They are known for their heavy weight and unique weaving technique using multiple ply yarns, including zari warp and twisted silk threads. The silk’s lustre is enhanced by the local water quality. Typically, two-ply yarn is used for the body and weft, and three-ply for borders, creating durable and richly textured sarees.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Painting
description: Kangra paintings are a classical art form from the Himalayan foothills, विकसित in the 18th century under royal patronage, especially Maharaja Sansar Chand. Originating from the Guler style, they are known for delicate, naturalistic, and lyrical depictions, often portraying themes from Krishna’s life. The paintings use natural pigments derived from minerals, plants, and organic sources, such as indigo, cinnabar, and malachite. Materials include handmade paper, natural gums as binders, and fine brushes made from animal hair. The technique emphasizes precise drawing, soft shading, and harmonious colour blending.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Shawl
description: Kani shawls are traditional woven textiles from Kashmir, known for intricate patterns created using a twill tapestry technique. The weaving involves interlocking weft yarns inserted with wooden spokes (kanis) without a shuttle, producing fine, lightweight, and durable shawls. Each shawl is made based on a detailed pattern script called ‘Talim,’ guiding skilled artisans. Designs feature motifs inspired by Kashmir’s flora, including paisley, floral, and chinar leaf patterns. The craft is practiced in regions like Srinagar and Budgam and involves multiple stages including dyeing, weaving, and finishing.

type of product: Non Food Products Other vegetal-based products / Perfume
description: Kannauj Perfume, also known as attar, is a traditional natural fragrance produced in Uttar Pradesh using hydro-distillation techniques. Made from flowers, herbs, and spices, these alcohol-free perfumes are valued for their long-lasting aroma and heritage linked to ancient perfumery practices.

type of product: Non Food Products Leather and leather based products / Saddlery
description: Kanpur Saddlery refers to high-quality leather goods produced in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, including saddles, harnesses, and equestrian equipment. Known for durability and fine craftsmanship, these products are made using traditional tanning and stitching methods.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Craft
description: Karnataka Bronzeware is a traditional metal craft involving the casting of bronze into idols, utensils, and decorative items. Produced using the lost-wax casting technique, these artifacts are known for their intricate detailing, durability, and cultural significance.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk
description: Karvath Kati Sarees and Fabrics are traditional silk textiles from Maharashtra characterized by distinctive serrated or zigzag border patterns. Woven using fine silk yarns, these sarees reflect a unique regional weaving style and vibrant color combinations.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton sarees
description: Kasaragod sarees are traditional cotton sarees produced using handloom weaving techniques, involving preparation of yarn and weaving on looms.

type of product: Non Food Products Other vegetal-based products / Paper mache craft
description: Kashmir papier-mache is a traditional craft involving molded paper pulp shaped into decorative objects and finished with intricate hand-painted designs.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Kashmir Pashmina is a traditional textile craft known for its fine quality and adaptability in garment design. It reflects the heritage and skill of Kashmiri artisans and contributes significantly to exports. The craft continues to evolve while maintaining its cultural significance and high demand in fashion.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Embroidery
description: Kashmir Sozani is a fine embroidery craft characterized by minute couching stitches used for outlining and filling motifs. Designs feature flora and fauna of the Kashmir Valley, such as chinar leaves, flowers, and fruits, using a subtle multi-colour palette known as Sofiyana Rang. Patterns include borders, butis, jaali (net-like designs), jamawar-style dense fillings, and large motifs like kunj. The process involves tracing designs onto fabric, filling them with fine stitches using dyed yarns, followed by washing and finishing to enhance lustre.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Carving wood craft
description: Kashmir walnut wood carving is a traditional craft developed over centuries and refined during the late 19th century with European influence. Using walnut wood (Juglans regia), known for its hardness, fine grain, and texture, artisans create detailed carvings featuring motifs inspired by local flora and fauna. The craft gained prominence under royal and colonial patronage and became an important export industry centered in Srinagar. Production involves seasoning wood for long periods, shaping by carpenters, detailed hand carving by skilled artisans, and finishing through polishing, resulting in decorative and functional objects.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Carpet
description: Kashmiri hand-knotted carpets originated in the 14th century with the introduction of skilled artisans by Mir Syed Ali Hamdani and flourished under Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin. These carpets are woven using a unique coded system called Taleem, which guides knotting patterns and colours. They feature intricate oriental and floral designs with motifs such as paisley, chinar tree, and tree-of-life. Made from combinations of silk, wool, and cotton, they are known for subtle colours and detailed craftsmanship. Production is carried out by skilled weavers, often working from home or in small units across Kashmir.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Embroidery
description: Kasuti Embroidery is a traditional hand embroidery form from Karnataka known for its intricate geometric patterns created using simple stitches without knots. Often worked on cotton fabrics, it features motifs inspired by temples, animals, and everyday life.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Puppet
description: Kathputlis of Rajasthan are traditional string puppets originating from the Nagaur district, used for entertainment, storytelling, and social commentary for generations. They are unique in that the strings are directly controlled by the puppeteer’s fingers without a control device, allowing complex movements. Puppets typically use 2 to 8 strings depending on size and function, and lack jointed hands. Production involves multiple steps including shaping and carving wooden parts such as the face using traditional tools and techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Khandua Saree and Fabrics are traditional handwoven textiles from Odisha made primarily from cotton or silk. Known for their tie-dye techniques and traditional motifs, these fabrics often feature inscriptions and cultural symbols woven into the design.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Building material
description: Khatamband is a traditional Kashmiri woodcraft used for ceilings and interior paneling, made by fitting small, intricately carved wooden pieces into grooved battens without nails or glue. The designs are based on geometric tessellations rooted in Islamic tradition and have a strong mathematical foundation. The structure is durable, reusable, and can be dismantled. Production is labour-intensive, involving seasoning wood, preparing geometric components, and assembling them using precise joinery techniques guided by master design scales passed through generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Pottery
description: Khurja Pottery is a renowned ceramic craft from Uttar Pradesh known for its brightly colored glazed pottery. Made using refined clay and fired in kilns, the products include decorative and utilitarian items featuring floral and geometric designs.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Toys
description: Kinhal toys are a traditional craft from Karnataka associated with the Vijayanagar Empire, inspired by temple art and supported by royal patronage. The craft uses wood combined with materials like tamarind seed paste (sari), adhesive mixtures (kitta), and surface coatings (bilidu) to shape and finish toys. Artisans apply cloth layers, natural and synthetic colours, and detailed painting, often using handmade brushes. The process includes assembling components, coating, smoothing, painting, and varnishing, resulting in decorative and durable folk toys.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Wool shawl
description: Kinnauri shawls are traditional textiles from Himachal Pradesh, woven as an integral part of daily life in Kinnaur households. They are made from various types of wool including local sheep wool, pashmina, and angora, as well as synthetic yarns. Weaving is done on pit looms or fly shuttle looms, with processes involving yarn preparation, warping, and weaving. The shawls are known for their intricate patterns and use of high-quality wool suited to cold climates.

type of product: Non Food Products Leather and leather based products / Footwear
description: Kolhapuri chappals are traditional handmade leather footwear originating from Maharashtra and Karnataka, with historical roots tracing back to the 12th century. Made from vegetable-tanned leather using eco-friendly processes, they are known for durability, water resistance, and comfort. Production involves tanning hides with natural materials like babul bark and myrobalan, followed by pattern making, cutting, shaping, stitching, and finishing. The craft is practiced by artisan communities and combines functionality with aesthetic appeal.

type of product: Non Food Products Extraction / Carving stone
description: Konark stone carving is a traditional craft from Odisha with origins dating back to the 6th–7th century, associated with temple architecture such as the Sun Temple. It uses materials like serpentine stone, sandstone, and granite, with serpentine being distinctive for its color and texture. The carvings often depict Odissi dance poses and traditional motifs. Production involves shaping stone blocks, rough carving, detailed chiseling, and finishing through polishing, using manual tools and techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Toys and figures
description: Kondapalli Bommallu are traditional wooden toys and figurines from Andhra Pradesh made using soft wood and natural dyes. Crafted by skilled artisans, these figures depict mythological scenes, rural life, and animals, reflecting cultural storytelling traditions.

Product name: Kosa silk Saree and Fabrics of Janjgir-Champa and Raigarh region
type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Kosa silk sarees from the Janjgir-Champa and Raigarh regions are traditionally woven textiles associated with tribal and handloom weaving communities, though the sector faces challenges due to limited institutional support.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Kota Doria is a traditional fabric from the Kota region of Rajasthan, with historical roots in fine cotton weaving that evolved into its distinctive check-patterned textile. The fabric is known for its lightweight, sheer texture and unique ‘khat’ check pattern created by combining cotton and silk yarns. It is woven on traditional pit looms using manual processes such as winding, warping, dyeing, sizing with natural onion-based starch, drafting, and weaving. The technique requires high skill to produce the characteristic square checks and soft yet textured finish.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Textile
description: Kotpad Handloom Fabric is a traditional textile from Odisha woven using natural vegetable dyes derived from local roots. Known for its earthy tones and tribal motifs, the fabric is produced on handlooms and reflects indigenous weaving practices.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton sarees
description: Kovai Kora cotton sarees originate from Coimbatore and are traditionally woven by the Devangar community, with historical links to the Vijayanagar Empire. These sarees combine silk warp and cotton weft, creating a distinctive blended fabric. Production involves processes such as yarn winding, dyeing, warp preparation, and weaving, with detailed work on pallu and motif designs. The sarees are known for their variety of colours, patterns, and the integration of ornamental motifs.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Woolen fabric
description: Kullu Shawls are traditional woolen textiles from Himachal Pradesh woven using sheep wool and known for their warmth and durability. Characterized by colorful geometric borders and intricate patterns, these shawls reflect the rich cultural heritage of the Kullu valley.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Embroidery
description: Kutch Embroidery is a traditional embroidery craft from Gujarat known for its intricate stitches, mirror work, and vibrant colors. Practiced by various communities, it features geometric and floral motifs and is used to decorate garments, textiles, and accessories.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton fabric
description: Kuthampally Dhoties and Set Mundu are handwoven cotton textiles from Kerala produced using traditional weaving techniques. Known for their fine texture, durability, and characteristic kasavu borders, these garments are widely used in traditional attire.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton sarees
description: Kuthampully sarees are traditional handloom textiles from Kerala associated with the Cochin dynasty and regional cultural practices. They are woven using fine count cotton yarns and are known for their quality craftsmanship and cultural significance in religious and festive occasions. Production involves processes such as winding, motif creation, weaving, and finishing, with quality inspection carried out by master weavers and supported by textile institutions.

type of product: Non Food Products / Animal-based fibres and textile / Woolen fabric - handicraft
description: Lahaul Socks and Gloves are handmade woolen products from Himachal Pradesh crafted using sheep and yak wool. Designed to provide insulation in cold climates, they feature traditional patterns and are knitted using indigenous techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products Leather and leather based products / Toys
description: Leather Toys of Indore are handcrafted items made from treated leather and natural dyes. These toys often depict animals and traditional figures, known for their durability, lightweight nature, and vibrant hand-painted designs.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Embroidery
description: Lucknow Chikan craft is a traditional embroidery technique from Uttar Pradesh, characterized by delicate hand embroidery on fabric using fine stitches to create intricate floral and geometric patterns.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Embroidery
description: Lucknow Zardozi is a traditional embroidery craft characterized by intricate metallic thread work, often using gold and silver threads to create elaborate decorative patterns on textiles.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Machilipatnam Kalamkari is a traditional hand block printing craft from Andhra Pradesh with historical roots linked to Golconda rule and international trade. It uses natural dyes derived from plant sources and involves processes such as bleaching, washing, dyeing, and resist printing. The craft is known for intricate Persian-influenced motifs, stylized flora and fauna, and a distinctive colour palette dominated by black, red, blue, yellow, and green. The quality of local water contributes to the vibrancy of colours.

type of product: Non Food Products Leather and leather based products / Percussion instrument
description: Maddalam is a traditional percussion instrument from Kerala, dating back to the 13th century and used in temple arts such as Kathakali and Panchavadyam. Made from a single block of jackfruit wood, it is hollowed into a cylindrical shape and fitted with cow and buffalo leather membranes. The instrument produces distinctive tones through a central black paste application and is crafted using specialized tools and techniques involving carving, shaping, and leather stretching.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Painting
description: Madhubani paintings originate from the Mithila region and are a traditional art form reflecting the cultural heritage of the area, historically used to decorate textiles and household items.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile
description: Madur Kathi is a traditional mat-weaving craft from West Bengal with origins tracing back to ancient India and references in early literature. It uses natural reed (Cyperus species) grown in swampy regions, processed into strips, dyed with natural vegetable dyes, and woven on looms. Different types such as ekrokha, dorokha, and masland vary in complexity and quality. The craft involves skilled manual weaving, often by multiple artisans, and features geometric and floral designs.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Flower
description: Madurai Malli is a variety of jasmine cultivated in the Madurai region, with historical references in ancient Tamil literature. It is known for its strong fragrance, thick petals, long shelf life, and suitability for garland making. The flowers are used in religious, cultural, and social contexts and can be preserved for longer durations compared to other varieties.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton sarees
description: Madurai Sungudi sarees are traditional cotton textiles from Tamil Nadu, dating back to the Nayak period. They are made using a unique tie-and-dye technique where intricate knots are tied on the fabric before dyeing, often exceeding thousands per saree. The process involves handcrafting by skilled artisans, with vegetable or chemical dyes and fine cotton yarns. The sarees are lightweight, breathable, and known for distinctive patterns, vibrant colours, and cultural significance.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Stone carving product
description: Mahabalipuram Stone Sculptures are traditional carvings from Tamil Nadu made using granite and other stones. Crafted by skilled artisans, these sculptures often depict deities, mythological figures, and temple art inspired by ancient Dravidian architecture.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: Maheshwar sarees and fabrics are traditional handloom textiles from Madhya Pradesh with a history of over 250 years, associated with the reign of Queen Ahilyabai Holkar. Made using silk, cotton, and zari, the production involves processes such as yarn selection, dyeing, warping, and weaving on handlooms. The sarees are known for their distinctive borders, lightweight texture, and fine craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Extraction / Marble
description: Makrana Marble is a high-quality white marble from Rajasthan known for its purity, strength, and fine texture. Widely used in architecture and sculpture, it is notably used in the construction of historic monuments such as the Taj Mahal.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton fabric
description: Mangalagiri sarees and fabrics are traditional cotton textiles from Andhra Pradesh, known for their durable, soft texture and characteristic Nizam borders with geometric designs. Made using 80s count cotton yarn on pit looms, they feature tightly woven structures that provide sheen and strength. The fabrics typically lack body motifs and emphasize borders, with occasional check patterns created through yarn arrangement. Production involves processes such as yarn purification, dyeing, winding, sizing with rice starch, and weaving on pit looms using skilled manual techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products / Others
description: Manjusha Art is a traditional folk painting style from Bihar characterized by bold lines, vibrant colors, and mythological themes. Typically created on paper or walls, it depicts stories associated with local folklore and religious narratives.

type of product: Non Food Products / Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees - handicraft
description: Mau Sarees are traditional textiles from Uttar Pradesh known for their fine weaving and use of silk and cotton yarns. These sarees often feature intricate patterns, zari work, and are valued for their craftsmanship and elegance.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Scissors
description: Meerut scissors are traditional cutting tools from Uttar Pradesh with a history of over 140 years, known for durability, sharpness, and affordability. Made primarily from carbon steel or mild steel, often using recycled scrap metal, they can be resharpened and have a long lifespan. Production involves processes such as melting and shaping metal, forging or press cutting, assembling blades and handles, and finishing with plating or polishing.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Carpet
description: Mirzapur handmade dari is a traditional woven floor covering from Uttar Pradesh, with origins linked to Mughal-era carpet weaving influenced by Persian designs. Made using cotton and wool yarns, the production involves design preparation, dyeing, warping, and weaving on looms using techniques such as the panja method. The finished products are used as floor coverings, mats, and upholstery, reflecting skilled craftsmanship passed down through generations.

type of product: Non Food Products / Metal / Metal handicraft - handicraft
description: Mirzapur Pital Bartan refers to traditional brass utensils crafted in Uttar Pradesh using casting and hammering techniques. Known for their durability and utility, these items include household vessels and decorative pieces reflecting local craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Mizo Puanchei is a traditional textile from Mizoram, evolved from the earlier Puanlaisen and known for its vibrant colours and intricate motifs. It is worn by women on special occasions and cultural performances such as the Cheraw dance. Traditionally woven on loin looms using cotton yarn dyed with natural substances, the fabric features warp-faced weaving with supplementary yarns for designs, though modern production also uses handlooms and synthetic or silk yarns.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Moirang Phee is a traditional textile from Manipur, featuring designs inspired by the ‘Pakhangba’ motif of local mythology. It is woven by women using extra weft techniques on loin, throw shuttle, or fly shuttle looms, producing distinctive patterned fabrics rooted in cultural traditions.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: Molakalmuru sarees are traditional silk textiles known for their distinctive contrast between the body and the border and pallu. The weaving uses multiple shuttles to create contrasting colours, with techniques such as Korvai used for border weaving. These sarees are produced using skilled handloom weaving and have a strong regional reputation.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Craft
description: Moradabad metal craft is a traditional industry known for brass and metal handicrafts, with historical influences from Persian, Turkish, and Egyptian designs. Production primarily uses sand casting, where molten metal is poured into molds, followed by processes such as chiseling, shaping, polishing, and electroplating. The craft involves both manual and mechanized techniques to produce decorative and functional metal items.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk
description: Muga silk is a traditional textile of Assam with historical use dating back to ancient times, produced from the silkworm Antheraea assamensis in the Brahmaputra Valley. Known for its natural golden-yellow colour, glossy texture, durability, and high tensile strength, its sheen increases with washing. Production involves rearing silkworms on host plants such as som and soalu, collecting cocoons, boiling and reeling fibres, followed by processes like starching, winding, warping, and weaving into fabrics.

type of product: Non Food Products Other vegetal-based products / Incense stick
description: Mysore Agarbathi is a traditional incense stick produced in Karnataka using natural ingredients such as sandalwood, resins, and aromatic oils. Known for its soothing fragrance and long-lasting aroma, it is widely used in religious rituals and meditation practices.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Jasmine flower
description: Mysore Malligae is a jasmine variety cultivated in Karnataka with historical use dating back centuries, known for its strong and long-lasting fragrance. Grown mainly in the Mysore and surrounding regions, its unique aroma is attributed to local geographical conditions and genetic characteristics. The flowers are widely used for garlands, especially in cultural and ceremonial occasions.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Craft
description: Mysore Rosewood Inlay is a traditional woodcraft from Karnataka involving intricate inlay work on rosewood surfaces using materials like ivory substitutes, bone, and colored wood. The craft features detailed patterns depicting floral designs, landscapes, and mythological scenes.

type of product: Non Food Products Other vegetal-based products / Soap
description: Mysore Sandal Soap is a traditional soap manufactured since 1918 in Karnataka, using pure vegetable oils and natural sandalwood oil. Known for its distinctive fragrance and quality, the production involves saponification of oils and fats with caustic soda, followed by drying, mixing with perfumes and additives, extrusion, cutting, and packaging. The soap is recognized for its biodegradable composition and long-lasting sandalwood aroma.

type of product: Non Food Products Other vegetal-based products / Oil
description: Mysore Sandalwood Oil is a traditional product originating from Karnataka since 1918, extracted from sandalwood grown in the region’s unique forest conditions. Known for its distinctive aroma and long-lasting fragrance, the oil is produced through processing and distillation of sandalwood, maintaining its high quality and global reputation.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk
description: Mysore silk is a traditional silk textile from Karnataka with origins dating back to the early 20th century, known for its quality and association with regulated production by state-run institutions.

type of product: Non Food Products Others / Painting
description: Mysore Traditional Paintings are classical artworks from Karnataka known for their elegance, muted colors, and fine detailing. Typically depicting Hindu deities and mythological themes, these paintings use natural pigments and gold leaf work on prepared surfaces.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Lamp
description: Nachiarkoil Kuthuvilakku is a traditional brass lamp from Tamil Nadu made using sand casting and wax moulding techniques. It involves preparing moulds from local sands, casting metal parts, assembling components through soldering, and finishing with shaping, polishing, and engraving. The craft uses materials like brass and clay cores, and requires skilled manual processes to produce decorative and functional lamps.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Nakshi Kantha is a traditional embroidery craft of Bengal made by layering old sarees or cloth and stitching them together with running stitches. It features intricate motifs of flora, fauna, and daily life, reflecting cultural and social themes. Traditionally created by women using recycled threads, each piece is unique and represents personal expression and regional heritage.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: Narayanpet sarees are characterized by a distinctive check pattern, with no additional floral, fauna, or other motifs. Their production follows a traditional weaving process unique to the region.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Carpet
description: Navalgund Durries are handwoven flat carpets from Karnataka made using cotton yarn on traditional looms. Known for their geometric patterns, durability, and reversible designs, these durries are commonly used as floor coverings and decorative textiles.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cloth
description: Ngotekherh is a traditional Mizo puan (cloth) historically worn by men and later by both genders, mainly during festivals and cultural occasions. Originating around the 18th century, it is woven with a white base and black stripes using loin or frame looms. Earlier made from homespun cotton dyed with natural dyes, modern versions use synthetic or acrylic yarns. The fabric features warp-faced plain weave with intricate techniques to conceal white weft under black warp, requiring high skill. Its quality is judged by the absence of white streaks, precision of stripes, and smoothness. The cloth is culturally significant and reflects traditional Mizo weaving practices.

type of product: Non Food Products Wood / Teak
description: Nilambur teak, sourced from plantations in Kerala, is historically significant as a major supplier of timber for British naval shipbuilding. Derived from Tectona grandis, it is known for its golden yellow to brown color, durability, stability, and resistance to weather, termites, and decay due to natural compounds like tectoquinone and naphthoquinone. The wood has high extractive content, straight grain, and excellent workability, making it ideal for shipbuilding, furniture, and structural uses. Its superior strength and dimensional stability have earned it global recognition.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Furniture
description: Nirmal furniture originated in the 17th century and later expanded to Hyderabad due to increased demand. Crafted from teak wood, the process involves carving, smoothing, priming, varnishing, and decorating with distinctive gold floral designs made using imported gold powder mixed with varnish. The furniture reflects a Nawabi aesthetic and is produced using traditional skills passed down through generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Painting
description: Nirmal paintings, developed since the 17th century and later expanded to Hyderabad, are created on wooden boards with a smooth, polished finish. The process involves preparing a teak wood frame, applying primer and lapam, and using synthetic colors. Designs are traced rather than freehand using perforation and chalk techniques, followed by detailed color filling. The paintings are known for their glossy finish and distinctive style.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Toys
description: Nirmal toys are traditionally crafted in Nirmal town of Adilabad district, Andhra Pradesh. The production is concentrated in specific villages within the region, where artisans have practiced this craft for generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Pottery
description: Nizamabad Black Pottery is a distinctive craft from Uttar Pradesh characterized by its glossy black finish and engraved silver designs. Made from locally sourced clay and fired in a reducing kiln, the pottery is both decorative and functional.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Orissa Ikat is a traditional resist-dye textile technique from Odisha where yarns are dyed before weaving to create intricate patterns. Known for its blurred edges and complex motifs, it is widely used in sarees and fabrics.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Painting cotton
description: Pattachitra is a traditional painting art from Odisha with ancient origins, named after cloth-based scrolls (patis). The process involves preparing treated cloth canvases using natural materials and executing detailed paintings, often depicting mythological themes. The production is carried out through a structured multi-step process rooted in traditional techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Paithani Sarees and Fabrics are luxurious silk textiles from Maharashtra known for their rich zari work and intricate motifs inspired by nature. Handwoven using fine silk and gold threads, these sarees are valued for their craftsmanship and vibrant colors.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Silk sarees
description: Patan Patola is a traditional double ikat silk weaving technique from Gujarat where both warp and weft threads are resist-dyed before weaving. Known for its precision, vibrant colors, and geometric patterns, it is considered one of the most intricate textile crafts in India.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Mat
description: Pattamadai mats are traditionally woven in Tamil Nadu using fine korai grass (Cyperus corymbosus) that grows along the Tamiraparani river, whose water, soil, and climate contribute to the grass’s quality. The craft originated with local artisans and evolved through generations, producing exceptionally fine mats that can be folded like cloth. The process involves harvesting, drying, splitting, dyeing, and weaving the grass on floor looms using a basket weave technique. Skilled craftsmanship produces soft, silk-like mats, with quality determined by the fineness of strands and weave density.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton cloth
description: Pawndum is a traditional Mizo cloth with deep cultural significance, historically used in rituals, ceremonies, and daily life. Originating around the 18th century, it evolved from simple white cloth to designs with black, red, and later multicolored bands using natural dyes. Traditionally woven by women on loin looms using homespun cotton, modern versions use synthetic yarns and advanced looms. It features a warp-faced plain weave with multicolored bands on a dark background. The cloth is used in festivals, dances, marriage customs, and funeral rites, reflecting its cultural importance.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Jewellery
description: Payyannur Pavithra Ring is a traditional ornament crafted by artisans under the guidance of hereditary families, with its production continuing through established cultural practices.

type of product: Non Food Products Metal / Craft
description: Pembarthi metal craft is an ancient brass craft from Telangana, known for its intricate designs and long history. The process involves preparing a lac base (lakka), fixing metal sheets, sketching and carving designs using specialized tools, followed by acid cleaning, filing, and polishing. Artisans use skilled techniques, including soldering and detailing, to create decorative items with fine craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Printing blocks
description: Pethapur printing blocks are traditional hand-carved wooden blocks from Gujarat, historically used for textile printing and associated with trade in Saudagiri fabrics. Made primarily from teak wood, the blocks are crafted through processes including seasoning, design tracing, engraving, and oil treatment for durability. Designs often feature geometric and floral motifs, requiring high precision and skilled craftsmanship. The craft, practiced for around two centuries, is known for its intricate workmanship and cultural significance.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk embroidery
description: Phulkari is a traditional embroidery style from Punjab characterized by dense floral patterns stitched using silk threads on coarse cotton fabric. The craft is known for its vibrant colors and is commonly used in shawls, dupattas, and garments.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Craft
description: Pipli appliqué work from Odisha is a traditional craft associated with the Jagannath temple, practiced mainly by the Darji community in Pipli and Puri. Historically used for religious canopies and festival items, the craft involves intricate patchwork and embroidery using techniques such as chain stitch and hemstitch. It is labor-intensive and reflects high technical skill and creativity, with its development closely linked to temple traditions.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Pochampalli Ikat is a traditional textile from Telangana made using cotton or silk yarns that are tied and dyed before weaving. The process involves precise tying, dyeing, and loom weaving to create characteristic patterns, typically featuring diamond or geometric motifs with diffused edges. The craft requires advanced skill in pattern visualization and coordinated teamwork, resulting in distinctive designs produced through traditional resist-dyeing techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Pottery
description: Pokaran pottery from Rajasthan includes both glazed and unglazed terracotta products made by traditional potter communities. Originally focused on household items like matkas and kulhars, the craft has expanded to decorative items such as vases, planters, and figurines. It is characterized by a distinctive light pink to near-white color achieved through careful processing of clay, including grinding, sieving, and kiln firing. The products combine utility and aesthetic appeal and are widely used in rural and urban settings.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Turban
description: Puneri Pagadi is a traditional headgear from Maharashtra dating back to the 17th century, historically made by Kostis. Typically made from cotton, and sometimes silk or satin, it features a structured form with elements like Koka, Jartar, and Jari decorations. The pagadi is prepared using starched fabric shaped manually, ensuring durability for limited use. Its distinct style, including the positioning of decorative elements, reflects cultural identity and traditional craftsmanship.

type of product: Non Food Products Processed minerals / Masks
description: Purulia Chau masks from West Bengal are integral to the Chau dance tradition and depict mythological characters through vivid colors and expressive designs. Made using clay, paper, cloth, and natural materials, the process involves creating a clay mold, layering with paper and cloth, shaping features, drying, and applying zinc oxide before painting and decoration. Masks are adorned with beads, feathers, foil, and other materials, with colors and expressions representing specific characters. The craft reflects local culture, skilled artistry, and traditional techniques passed through generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Sarees
description: Rajkot Patola is a single ikat silk weaving tradition from Gujarat where either warp or weft threads are resist-dyed to create patterns. Known for its vibrant designs and comparatively simpler technique than double ikat, it is widely used in sarees and dress materials.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Craft
description: Saharanpur wood craft is a traditional carving industry in Uttar Pradesh known for intricate designs on woods like sheesham, teak, and mango. The craft includes carved, inlaid, and engraved products such as furniture, decorative items, and utility goods. It combines traditional floral and nature-inspired motifs with influences from other regional styles. The process involves seasoning wood, carving, engraving, and finishing, with both handcrafted and machine-assisted techniques used for domestic and international markets.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Fabric
description: Salem fabric is part of a long-standing textile tradition in Tamil Nadu, associated with continuous production over centuries.

type of product: Non Food Products Animal-based fibres and textile / Silk
description: Salem silk is a traditional textile from Tamil Nadu with a long history linked to regional weaving communities. Known for its lustrous white silk dhoties, the fabric’s quality is attributed to local water used in processing, which enhances its sheen. Produced using fly shuttle and throw shuttle looms, the silk incorporates materials such as silk yarn, zari, and colored threads. The weaving requires precision to achieve dense texture and distinctive bordered designs.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton sarees
description: Sambalpuri Bandha textiles from Odisha are created using a traditional tie-and-dye (ikat) technique where designs are formed on yarn before weaving. The craft features intricate geometric and curvilinear motifs such as flowers, animals, and cultural symbols, often visible on both sides of the fabric. Both single and double ikat styles are practiced using cotton and silk. The process is labor-intensive, involving precise tying, dyeing, and weaving, resulting in vibrant, detailed patterns.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Embroidery
description: Sandur Lambani embroidery is a traditional craft of the Lambani community in Karnataka, characterized by bright colors, non-figurative patterns, and extensive embellishments. It combines stitching, patchwork, appliqué, and mirror work on cotton or silk fabrics, often decorated with beads, shells, coins, tassels, and metal ornaments. The process involves dyeing, pattern marking, hand embroidery by artisans, and finishing with additional decorative elements. The craft reflects the community’s nomadic heritage and is preserved through collective artisan practices.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Printing
description: Sanganeri hand block printing is a traditional textile printing craft from Rajasthan with a history spanning over 300 years, known for its detailed hand-carved block designs and fine printing techniques.

type of product: Non Food Products Wooden products / Furniture
description: Sankheda furniture from Gujarat is a traditional craft with origins linked to migrating artisans and centuries-old lacquer techniques. Made primarily from seasoned teak wood, it is characterized by turned wood forms, vibrant painted surfaces, and lacquered finishes with floral and geometric motifs. The production involves shaping wood on a lathe, smoothing, applying primer, hand-painting designs, and finishing with lacquer using heat and polishing. The furniture is known for its durability, strength, and distinctive glossy appearance, achieved through skilled craftsmanship passed down generations.

type of product: Non Food Products Leather and leather based products / Craft
description: Santiniketan leather goods, developed in West Bengal since 1932 under Rathindranath Tagore, are handcrafted using vegetable-tanned leather. Known for their glossy finish and embossed designs, the products feature traditional motifs and retain permanent impressions. The process involves preparing leather, cutting, embossing or batik dyeing with natural dyes, glazing, assembling with linings and accessories, and finishing. The craft emphasizes detailed manual techniques and distinctive aesthetic qualities.

type of product: Non Food Products Vegetal-based fibres and textile / Cotton sarees
description: Santipur sarees from West Bengal are traditional cotton textiles known for fine texture achieved through balanced warp and weft density. They feature floral, geometric, and cultural motifs, often with distinctive borders and pallus.
